Practitioner-sourced synthesis (Lenny's Podcast, YC, Hormozi, Reddit founder threads, investor talks). The operational layer beneath the canon's conceptual books — maps to Course 10 (Entrepreneurship & Venture) and the Product Thinking & Innovation cluster (canon ries lean startup, canon thiel zero to one, canon cagan inspired). Banked 2026-06-06.

1 · Getting to product-market fit

  • "Interesting" is a polite no. Only "wow" + behavior counts — "I'd sign up today," "can we meet next week?" Reinhardt (Segment): 4 of 5 "that's great, makes sense" = doesn't care.
  • Willingness-to-pay = actually charge, raising price until they wince but still pay (Ramanujam's fair→expensive→prohibitive ladder; "expensive" is the real number). Reinhardt asked $120K, closed $18K.
  • Best customer is already failing to build the fix themselves — has budget, is shopping vendors. Ironclad's break: one-line cold email "Are you a CLM?" to someone evaluating 10–12 tools.
  • Sell before you build. Lattice sold its first 5–10 on Figma mockups; Vanta manually filled a spreadsheet pretending to be the AI. Extreme satisfaction first, efficiency later (Cagan-style discovery).
  • Pick the wedge where customers hack your product, not where your vision points. Segment found its real product when 5 customers independently described the same unprompted workflow.
  • Quant bar: Sean Ellis test — 40% "very disappointed" if it vanished. Track cohort renewal + NRR, not signups. "$1M ARR a month after launch is ZERO proof of PMF."
  • When stuck, 200% pivot, not 10% — change Persona / Problem / Promise / Product. Plaid kept its code, flipped persona consumers→fintech devs. (See canon ries lean startup pivot-or-persevere.)

2 · Founding team & early hires

  • The killer is relationship, not skill. YC: never hears "my cofounder lacks skills"; always "my cofounder is a nightmare." Pick someone you've fought with and like over a perfect-skill stranger.
  • Avoid 50/50 deadlock — near-equal but give the CEO one extra share as a written tiebreaker.
  • Always vest: 4 years, 1-year cliff. Else a cofounder who quits month 8 keeps a frozen cap-table slice.
  • Too little conflict is the silent killer. Garry Tan resigned from Posterous (10× growth) at resting pulse 120 because he and his cofounder stopped talking. Tell: you don't hang out outside work.
  • "Fighting about everything" = undefined roles. Heroku gave every task one owner whose ass was on the line, then disagree-and-commit. (Echoes canon bezos shareholder letters / canon alchian demsetz firm.)
  • Equity only for money, skills, or time you genuinely lack. Hormozi (9 failed partnerships): run a prospective partner through lawyers/contract first as a stress test.

3 · Unit economics before scale

  • LTV uses lifetime gross profit, not revenue. Hormozi: a $2,000/mo client netted $0 after ad + mgmt.
  • LTV:CAC ≥ 3:1 (near-universal). Below = costs too high or churn too fast.
  • CAC payback < 12 mo (ideally 6–9). Even 3:1 bankrupts you if payback exceeds runway.
  • Formulas: LTV = (ARPU × gross margin) ÷ churn; payback = CAC ÷ (ARPU × gross margin). Target 65%+ gross margin (80%+ SaaS). (Ties to learn/unit-04 health + canon klarman margin of safety.)
  • Watch contribution margin. Uber was −$0.22/ride after driver pay/incentives — "make it up on volume" is the trap.
  • Price is the highest-leverage lever: a ~10% price bump barely dents conversion, falls straight to profit (one case: profit/customer $40→$64, +63%). (See canon shapiro varian information rules.)

4 · Distribution & go-to-market

  • First 100 come from personal network (51%) + 1:1 outreach (50%). SEO/content (~9%), Product Hunt (~4%) rarely produce early traction. YC: "startups don't take off by themselves — manually recruit."
  • Match channel to user. Cold email to tradespeople ≈ 4% reply; texts/Nextdoor/local FB/BNI work. Creator/affiliate endorsements convert ~10× cold for low-trust audiences.
  • First 20–30 sales calls = research, not pitches — find the one-sentence trigger that makes prospects "light up." One founder: 0→sale-in-11-days after recutting ICP to "solo founders who just hired their first salesperson."
  • Frustrated users are highest-converting — reply personally, fix the bug same-day.
  • Data, not pitches, earns attention — "only 7 of 2,500 agency sites scored above 90" outperformed daily promo. SEO compounds only if you write to the panic-moment query.

5 · When/whether to raise (or not)

  • VC needs 100–1,000×. A profitable $5M/yr business is a failure by their math — "don't put jet fuel in a Toyota Camry." (See canon bezos shareholder letters capital allocation.)
  • Dilution can invert outcomes: two bootstrappers split a $50M exit → $25M each; after YC+seed+A+B, a $200M exit pays each only ~$20M.
  • "Google rule": only raise when you literally can't exist otherwise. Raising sells freedom.
  • Below ~50% ownership (≈Series B) the board can set your salary and fire you (Kalanick is structural, not a freak event). (See canon jensen meckling agency theory control.)
  • Deadliest failure = "between-rounds death" — pre-seed must fund you to a fundable milestone + buffer.
  • VC incentive is misaligned — they want you to "light capital on fire"; ~2 of 20 bets carry the fund.
  • Counterpoint: only ~6% of Fortune 500 were VC-funded; non-dilutive capital is an underused middle path.

6 · Operational scaling pain

  • "If you build it, they will come" is the #1 scaling killer — you're in the sales business first.
  • Overbuilding before PMF > underbuilding. Scope creep disguised as iteration (widget → analytics platform in 5 weeks, never nailing one job) silently kills. (Anti-pattern to canon cagan inspired.)
  • Self-inflicted wounds: limiting hiring to your own country; pitching investors before traction.

7 · Moat & defensibility

  • Track the moat's direction, not its size today. Only widening gross margin / pricing power / cohort engagement is durable. "If you can spot it easily, it probably doesn't exist." (See canon helmer 7 powers.)
  • Ultimate moat: deliberately crash your own gross margin so no competitor can profitably enter (Amazon Basics, Jio). Virality and capital are NOT moats (Clubhouse had both, ~zero switching costs).
  • Build the demand side; supply gets sucked in. Canva (high standalone utility) → $6B while Shutterstock (utility tied to supply) → ~$1.7B. (See canon parker platform revolution, canon hagiu wright multi sided platforms.)
  • Underrated buildable moats: customer-controlled switching costs; concierge service (Zappos).

8 · The other seat — how VCs think (the investor-side mirror)

Everything above is the founder's seat. The allocator's seat is in harlem capital vc insights (Henri Pierre-Jacques / Brandon Bryant, Harlem Capital — 17 videos). The pairings that matter most: - "Is it venture?" — VCs reject great cash-flow businesses as "not venture" (need $100M–$1B+ via IPO/acquisition + 50%+ growth). A "no" is often a classification, not a judgment. (↔ §5.) - Fund size dictates the check — sub-$50M funds run 5–8% ownership; $100M+ funds must own 10–20%, so a small check from a big fund breaks their math. Match your raise to their portfolio construction. (↔ §5.) - LPs buy process over a lucky home run; carry is $0 if the fund misses full-carry mode (European waterfall: LPs whole first → 8% hurdle → catch-up → 80/20). Markups are leading indicators that can evaporate 70%. This is why VCs push for 100–1,000× and "light capital on fire." (↔ §5.) - Brand/trust is sourcing — VCs "track founders for years before they have a company"; be the first call. "Document, don't create." (↔ "distribution is the new moat" below.)

Two cross-cutting patterns

  • Distribution is the new moat — AI makes the product easy; getting attention is the defensible part.
  • Sell the outcome, not the mechanism — "post a job photo, Google finds your next customer" beat "feed-first website builder with auto-indexing." Same product, opposite conversion. (See canon sinek start with why, canon duarte resonate.)
